newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax authorities search DG Bank.
newsitem.headline: German tax authorities search DG Bank.

text.p: Germany's DG Bank Deutsche Genossenchaftsbank was searched by around 100 tax authority officials on Monday on suspicion the bank had aided customers to evade taxes by transferring funds to Luxembourg, DG said.

A spokesman for the bank confirmed in answer to Reuter enquiries that the searches were taking place and added that they could take several days. "The prosecutors office told us that the search could take days," he said.
The search followed a ruling by the Bielefeld district court, the spokesman said, adding that DG Bank has given assurances that it would work together with the authorities to clear up the problem.
The company's headquarters in Frankfurt and the offices of several cooperative banks (Volks- und Raiffeisenbanken) in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia had been searched, he said.
DG Bank is head of the German cooperative banking group, which, in common with several other major German banks, has already faced suspicion of aiding tax evasion in some areas.

The banks are accused of having encouraged customers to move funds abroad to evade a withholding tax. Investing abroad is legal but individuals break the law if they do not declare their financial gains in Germany.
